findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. Line 304 passes only `fail` or `unknown` to `_item_readiness`. A clean item from an earlier release with green checks and no ready receipt cannot reach that function's older-release readiness path, which requires `checks == "pass"` (`src/forge/nextstep.py:634-639`); it can be held behind an overlapping item despite being ready. A required check that reports skipped is also treated as `unknown` here, although Forge counts a skipped required check as failed (`src/forge/checks.py:124-132`). Such an item incorrectly bypasses the hold.
findings.title: Not done: use Forge's check status for the overlap bypass

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Test. The assertion turns the timed entries into sets, so reversing the first two closes still passes. `_in_close` also takes each child's second pull-request lookup as its close entry time, but that lookup occurs in `land._merged` before the child prints `Closing` and enters close (`src/forge/land.py:57-79`). The named oldest-first close-start behavior remains unproved by the timed log.
findings.title: Not done: test_1 proves the closes start oldest first

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Test. The only pre-existing stop in test_4 is a fresh review-loop stop. It never runs `forge land --all` after the 30-minute default becomes due or with a worker-stuck stop containing `stop.question`. The test would pass if the queue ceased applying the default on a later run or gave a worker-stuck change the review-loop question and wrong resolve step. Both are named stop behaviors in item 4.
findings.title: Not done: test_4 proves the later default and worker-stuck stops
